# Per-document cloud-controls-matrix citation validity

A CSA Cloud Controls Matrix (CCM) or AI Controls Matrix (AICM) control-code
citation in a corpus document resolves to a real entry in the authoritative
CCM/AICM catalogue, and its cited title fits that entry. The check validates a
``DOMAIN-NN`` control token wherever it appears (the domain prefix must be a real
matrix domain, and the control number must fall within that domain's range), and
adds several context-scoped checks: a bare known-bad domain token in a CCM/AICM
context (a superseded v4.0 domain code named as a current citation, distinct from
a rename-note or supersession line, which is exempt); a framework-alignment-table
column whose header names the matrix, whose body cells are then read as codes; a
framework-label row whose cited title must match the catalogue title; a bare
domain given an inline or column title that must fit the catalogue's domain title;
and a section-aware cross-catalogue title check that catches a control cited under
one matrix's section but carrying the other matrix's title (a handful of controls
share a code across CCM and AICM with slightly different titles, which the
conservative content-word title check alone cannot separate). Codes inside fenced
code blocks, corpus-internal identifiers with a leading or trailing hyphen (the
``MODEL-GOV-NN`` / ``AI-GOV-NN`` family), and non-matrix uses of the same letters
(``.NET``, currency codes, prose) are not matched. The reference catalogue (the
valid domains and their control ranges, the known-bad domains, the CCM and AICM
title maps, and the domain names) is supplied by the adopter and is not part of
this clause; the central compliance matrix is validated by a separate check and is
out of this check's scan scope by that check's own configuration. A document whose
CCM/AICM citations are all valid and correctly-titled contributes no findings.
